sections.description: This section establishes the foundational knowledge of Behçet’s disease (BD), its systemic manifestations, and the specific characteristics of its neurological involvement (neuro-BD), providing the necessary background to understand the complexity of the case.
subtopics: Epidemiology and clinical features of systemic Behçet’s Disease
International Criteria for Behçet’s Disease (point system)
Pathophysiology of neuro-Behçet’s disease (neuro-BD)
Typical vs. acute presentations of neuro-BD (meningoencephalitis vs. parenchymal lesions)
The role (and limitations) of HLA-B51 in diagnosis

sections.description: This section focuses on the initial presentation of the patient, highlighting the non-specific symptoms and the importance of recognizing electrolyte disturbances as potential clues to underlying systemic inflammation.
subtopics: Analysis of mucocutaneous findings (oral aphthae, folliculitis-like rashes, genital ulcers)
Identifying non-specific neurological and systemic symptoms (headache, fever, arthralgia)
Interpreting severe hyponatraemia in a febrile patient
Recognizing 'red flag' complications of hyponatraemia: hiccups and rhabdomyolysis
The challenge of concurrent diagnosis of systemic and neurological BD

sections.description: This section details the systematic process of excluding other conditions that mimic neuro-BD and SIADH, illustrating the clinician's logic in navigating a complex diagnostic picture.
subtopics: Excluding infectious causes: Bacterial, viral (HSV/VZV), and tuberculous meningitis
Ruling out primary CNS malignancies and haematological disorders
Evaluating other systemic inflammatory diseases: Sarcoidosis and autoimmune markers
Interpreting CSF analysis: Aseptic meningitis and inflammatory markers
Radiological interpretation: Understanding normal brain MRI in early neuro-BD

sections.description: This section explores the specific complication of Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone secretion (SIADH) within the context of neuro-BD, focusing on the underlying immunological mechanisms.
subtopics: Mechanism of SIADH: Dysregulated ADH secretion in CNS inflammation
The role of proinflammatory cytokines: IL-6 and its mediation of ADH release
Monocyte activation and cytokine production in Behçet’s Disease
Laboratory confirmation of SIADH: Osmolality, urinary sodium, and ADH levels
Management principles of SIADH: Fluid restriction and sodium monitoring

sections.description: The final section discusses the treatment decisions made in this case, comparing standard therapies with the specific use of colchicine monotherapy, and summarizes the clinical pearls for future practice.
subtopics: Standard pharmacotherapy for neuro-BD (Corticosteroids and immunosuppressants)
Mechanism of action of Colchicine: Neutrophil inhibition and cytokine suppression
Clinical review of colchicine as a potential therapy for acute neuro-BD
Analysis of the patient's outcome and long-term stabilization
Key takeaways: Recognizing neuro-BD in patients with concurrent SIADH and mucocutaneous features
